questions.stem: What role is used in the organization account to perform all organization-level tasks?

options.text: ORGADMIN
ACCOUNTADMIN
GLOBALORGADMIN
SYSADMIN

explanation.correct: The GLOBALORGADMIN role in the organization account is used to perform all organization-level tasks, including account management and access to premium views.

distractors.A: ORGADMIN is the legacy role in ORGADMIN-enabled regular accounts and is being phased out for multi-account organizations.
distractors.B: ACCOUNTADMIN is the highest-level role within a single account but does not manage organization-level tasks.
distractors.D: SYSADMIN manages databases and warehouses within an account, not organization-level operations.

questions.stem: Which Snowflake edition is required to use the organization account feature?

options.text: Standard
Business Critical
Virtual Private Snowflake (VPS)
Enterprise

explanation.correct: The organization account is an Enterprise Edition feature (or higher). Standard Edition does not support organization accounts.

distractors.A: Standard Edition does not include the organization account capability.
distractors.B: Business Critical supports it because it is higher than Enterprise, but Enterprise is the minimum required edition.
distractors.C: VPS supports it as a higher edition, but Enterprise is the minimum requirement.

questions.stem: How is a Snowflake organization created for customers who sign up using the self-service option?

options.text: The customer must submit a request to Snowflake Support
An organization is automatically created with a system-generated name
The customer creates it manually using the CREATE ORGANIZATION command
The organization is created only after purchasing Enterprise Edition

explanation.correct: For users who sign up via the self-service option, an organization is automatically created with a system-generated name when the account is created.

distractors.A: Contacting Snowflake Support is only relevant for entities who work directly with Snowflake personnel to set up accounts with custom names.
distractors.C: Snowflake customers never directly create an organization; it is always created by Snowflake automatically or by Snowflake personnel.
distractors.D: Organization creation is not tied to a specific edition purchase — it happens automatically at account sign-up.

questions.stem: Which of the following are types of accounts that can exist within a Snowflake organization? (Select THREE)

options.text: Reader account administrator account
Regular Snowflake account
Snowflake Open Catalog account
Data warehouse account
Organization account
Replication controller account

explanation.correct: An organization can consist of three types of accounts: organization accounts (used by organization administrators), regular Snowflake accounts (including trial accounts), and Snowflake Open Catalog accounts (used to manage catalogs in Snowflake Open Catalog).

distractors.A: Reader accounts exist but are a subtype of regular accounts, not a distinct account type at the organization level.
distractors.D: There is no separate 'data warehouse account' type — warehouses exist within regular accounts.
distractors.F: There is no 'replication controller account' type. Replication is a feature managed through the organization account.

questions.stem: Which privileges can the GLOBALORGADMIN role assign to other roles in the organization account? (Select THREE)

options.text: CREATE DATABASE
MANAGE ACCOUNTS
MANAGE ORGANIZATION TERMS
MANAGE WAREHOUSES
IMPORT SHARES
APPLY TAG

explanation.correct: The GLOBALORGADMIN role can assign MANAGE ACCOUNTS, APPLY TAG, MANAGE LISTING AUTO FULFILLMENT, MANAGE ORGANIZATION CONTACTS, MANAGE ORGANIZATION TERMS, and PURCHASE DATA EXCHANGE LISTING to other roles.

distractors.A: CREATE DATABASE is an account-level privilege, not an organization-level privilege assignable by GLOBALORGADMIN.
distractors.D: MANAGE WAREHOUSES is not an organization-level privilege — warehouses are managed within individual accounts.
distractors.E: IMPORT SHARES is not one of the assignable organization-level privileges.

questions.stem: Which of the following are benefits of Snowflake organizations? (Select TWO)

options.text: Shared warehouse resources across all accounts
Automatic performance tuning across all accounts
A central view of all accounts within the organization
Self-service account creation within the organization
Automatic data deduplication between accounts

explanation.correct: Organizations provide self-service account creation and a central view of all accounts, along with data replication/failover, cross-region data sharing, and organization-wide usage monitoring.

distractors.A: Warehouse resources are not shared across accounts — each account has its own warehouses.
distractors.B: Organizations do not provide automatic performance tuning — each account manages its own performance independently.
distractors.E: Data deduplication between accounts is not a feature of organizations.

questions.scenario: A large enterprise has recently adopted Snowflake and is setting up their organization. The security team wants to monitor usage data from all accounts in a single location, including query history from each account.
questions.stem: Which feature should the enterprise use to access organization-level data collected from all accounts?

options.text: ACCOUNT_USAGE schema in any regular account
Premium views in the organization account's ORGANIZATION_USAGE schema
INFORMATION_SCHEMA in the organization account
READER_ACCOUNT_USAGE schema

explanation.correct: Premium views in the organization account's ORGANIZATION_USAGE schema provide organization-level data aggregated from all accounts, including query history that isn't otherwise available in a single view.

distractors.A: ACCOUNT_USAGE only provides data for the specific account you are querying, not across all accounts.
distractors.C: INFORMATION_SCHEMA provides metadata about objects in the current database, not organization-wide usage data.
distractors.D: READER_ACCOUNT_USAGE is not a real schema — reader accounts are managed within provider accounts.

questions.scenario: A company has been using the ORGADMIN role in a regular account to manage their multi-account organization. They received a notification from Snowflake about upcoming changes.
questions.stem: What is Snowflake's recommendation regarding the ORGADMIN role for multi-account organizations?

options.text: Continue using ORGADMIN as it provides more granular control
Migrate to using the GLOBALORGADMIN role in the organization account
Replace ORGADMIN with ACCOUNTADMIN in each account
Create a custom role to replace ORGADMIN functionality

explanation.correct: Using the ORGADMIN role in an ORGADMIN-enabled account is being phased out. Snowflake recommends using the GLOBALORGADMIN role in the organization account to perform organization-level tasks.

distractors.A: Snowflake is phasing out the ORGADMIN role, not recommending continued use.
distractors.C: ACCOUNTADMIN cannot perform organization-level tasks and is not a replacement for ORGADMIN.
distractors.D: Custom roles cannot replace ORGADMIN — the GLOBALORGADMIN role in the organization account is the designated replacement.

questions.scenario: An organization administrator needs to enable the ORGADMIN role in a second account called 'analytics_prod'. They are currently logged into an account that already has the ORGADMIN role enabled.
questions.stem: Which SQL command should the administrator execute to enable the ORGADMIN role in the analytics_prod account?

options.text: GRANT ROLE ORGADMIN TO ACCOUNT analytics_prod;
ALTER ACCOUNT analytics_prod SET IS_ORG_ADMIN = TRUE;
CREATE ROLE ORGADMIN IN ACCOUNT analytics_prod;
ALTER ACCOUNT analytics_prod ENABLE ORGADMIN;

explanation.correct: The ALTER ACCOUNT command with SET IS_ORG_ADMIN = TRUE enables the ORGADMIN role in the specified account. This must be executed from an account that already has ORGADMIN enabled.

distractors.A: GRANT ROLE is used to grant roles to users, not to enable the ORGADMIN role in an account.
distractors.C: The ORGADMIN role is not created manually — it is enabled on accounts using ALTER ACCOUNT.
distractors.D: The correct syntax uses SET IS_ORG_ADMIN = TRUE, not ENABLE ORGADMIN.

questions.scenario: A financial institution has a hybrid organization with accounts in both a U.S. SnowGov Region and a commercial region. They are planning to create an organization account.
questions.stem: What does Snowflake recommend for organizations with accounts in both regulated and non-regulated regions?

options.text: Create the organization account in the commercial region for cost savings
Create separate organization accounts for each region
Create the organization account in the regulated region
Avoid creating an organization account and use ORGADMIN only

explanation.correct: For hybrid organizations, Snowflake recommends creating the organization account in the regulated region to ensure metadata stays within compliance boundaries.

distractors.A: Creating in a commercial region could violate compliance requirements by moving metadata from regulated accounts to a non-regulated region.
distractors.B: Only one organization account can exist per organization — you cannot create separate ones per region.
distractors.D: ORGADMIN is being phased out, and an organization account is the recommended path forward.

questions.scenario: A company wants to change the name of their Snowflake organization and is evaluating what happens during and after the rename process.
questions.stem: Which statements about changing an organization name are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: The original account URL can be kept temporarily for up to 90 days if chosen
Organization renaming can be done via ALTER ORGANIZATION command
Renaming the organization immediately invalidates all existing account URLs
The organization can be renamed directly in Snowsight by the GLOBALORGADMIN
You must contact Snowflake Support to change the organization name

explanation.correct: Changing an organization name requires contacting Snowflake Support. When the name is changed, you can decide whether users can temporarily access accounts using the original account URL, which is automatically dropped after 90 days if kept.

distractors.B: There is no ALTER ORGANIZATION command — organization renaming requires Snowflake Support.
distractors.C: The original URL is not immediately invalidated — it can be kept for up to 90 days by choice.
distractors.D: Organization renaming cannot be done in Snowsight — it requires contacting Snowflake Support.

questions.scenario: An organization administrator wants to delete their Snowflake organization because the company is decommissioning all Snowflake resources.
questions.stem: Which steps are required to delete a Snowflake organization? (Select TWO)

options.text: Revoke GLOBALORGADMIN from all users first
Disable premium views before deletion
Execute DROP ORGANIZATION from the organization account
Delete all accounts in the organization except the one being used for the deletion
Contact Snowflake Support to delete the last account and the organization

explanation.correct: To delete an organization, you must first delete all accounts except one, then contact Snowflake Support to delete the last account and the organization itself.

distractors.A: Revoking GLOBALORGADMIN is not a prerequisite for organization deletion.
distractors.B: Disabling premium views is not a required step for organization deletion.
distractors.C: There is no DROP ORGANIZATION command — the final deletion requires Snowflake Support.

questions.scenario: A global organization administrator wants to create a new organization account. They have an existing account with ORGADMIN enabled and are considering which account to use as the basis for creating the organization account.
questions.stem: Which statement is true about creating an organization account?

options.text: An existing regular account can be converted to the organization account
The CREATE ORGANIZATION ACCOUNT command must be executed from an ORGADMIN-enabled account
Multiple organization accounts can be created per organization for redundancy
The organization account can only be created by Snowflake Support

explanation.correct: To create the organization account, you must execute CREATE ORGANIZATION ACCOUNT from an existing account that has the ORGADMIN role enabled.

distractors.A: You cannot convert an existing ORGADMIN-enabled account to be the organization account — it must be created as a new account.
distractors.C: There is only one organization account per organization — multiple organization accounts are not supported.
distractors.D: Organization administrators can create the organization account themselves using the CREATE ORGANIZATION ACCOUNT command.

questions.scenario: An organization administrator is reviewing the Organization Hub in Snowsight to understand their organization's posture across multiple dimensions.
questions.stem: Which sections are available in the Organization Hub Insights dashboard? (Select THREE)

options.text: Query health
Security
Billing and Cost management
Data replication status
Warehouse auto-scaling metrics
User login frequency

explanation.correct: The Organization Hub Insights dashboard includes sections for Billing and Cost management, Security, and Query health (among others like Storage). These provide interactive tiles showing trends and alerts across all accounts.

distractors.D: Data replication status is not a section in the Organization Hub Insights dashboard.
distractors.E: Warehouse auto-scaling metrics is not a dedicated section in the Organization Hub.
distractors.F: User login frequency is not a section in the Organization Hub Insights dashboard.

questions.scenario: A company's compliance team is evaluating the premium views feature in the organization account and wants to understand its requirements and limitations.
questions.stem: Which statements about premium views in the organization account are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Premium views are fully populated immediately after the organization account is created
Premium views can be accessed from any regular account in the organization
Premium views incur additional costs based on how many records were processed
Premium views are available by default only in organizations with a capacity contract
Premium views are free for all Snowflake editions

explanation.correct: Premium views incur additional costs based on records processed, and by default they are only available in organizations that have a capacity contract. On-demand accounts must contact Snowflake Support to access them.

distractors.A: It can take two weeks from the time the organization account is created until premium views are fully populated with 365 days of historical data.
distractors.B: Premium views are only available in the ORGANIZATION_USAGE schema of the organization account, not in regular accounts.
distractors.E: Premium views are not free — they incur costs based on the number of records processed.

questions.scenario: A Snowflake administrator is trying to determine the maximum number of accounts that can have the ORGADMIN role enabled in their organization.
questions.stem: Which statements about the ORGADMIN role are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: The ORGADMIN role must be manually enabled for the first account in an organization
By default, the ORGADMIN role can be enabled in a maximum of eight accounts
The ORGADMIN role can be enabled for reader accounts
The first account in an organization has the ORGADMIN role enabled by default
The ORGADMIN role can be enabled in an unlimited number of accounts

explanation.correct: By default, the ORGADMIN role can be enabled in a maximum of eight accounts (contact support for more). The first account in an organization has the ORGADMIN role enabled automatically.

distractors.A: The first account automatically has the ORGADMIN role enabled — no manual action is needed.
distractors.C: The ORGADMIN role cannot be enabled for a reader account.
distractors.E: The default maximum is eight accounts — you must contact Snowflake Support to have this limit raised.

questions.scenario: An organization administrator notices that the Organization Hub is not accessible from their regular Snowflake account. They can see the Admin menu but not the Organization Hub option.
questions.stem: What is the most likely reason the Organization Hub is not available?

options.text: The administrator needs to enable it in Account Settings
The Organization Hub is only accessible from the organization account with GLOBALORGADMIN role and premium views enabled
The Organization Hub requires Business Critical edition
The feature must be enabled by Snowflake Support for each account

explanation.correct: The Organization Hub requires an organization account with premium views enabled. It is accessed by signing into the organization account and switching to the GLOBALORGADMIN role.

distractors.A: There is no Account Settings toggle for the Organization Hub — it is inherently tied to the organization account.
distractors.C: The Organization Hub requires an organization account (Enterprise or higher), not specifically Business Critical.
distractors.D: The Organization Hub does not require per-account enablement by Snowflake Support — it is available automatically in the organization account.

questions.scenario: An organization administrator is considering the implications of having a hybrid organization where some accounts are in a U.S. SnowGov Region and others are in commercial regions.
questions.stem: What recommendations does Snowflake make for hybrid organizations? (Select TWO)

options.text: Use separate organizations for regulated and non-regulated accounts
Place all accounts in the same region to avoid compliance issues
Create the organization account in the regulated region
Disable premium views to prevent metadata movement between regions
Do not define organization-level objects with sensitive or regulated data

explanation.correct: Snowflake recommends creating the organization account in the regulated region and not defining organization-level objects with sensitive or regulated data, since metadata might move between regions.

distractors.A: Snowflake does not recommend separate organizations — they recommend creating the organization account in the regulated region.
distractors.B: Snowflake supports multi-region organizations and does not require all accounts be in the same region.
distractors.D: Snowflake does not recommend disabling premium views — instead, they recommend proper placement of the organization account.

questions.scenario: A newly hired Snowflake platform engineer needs to understand what tiles are available in the Billing and Cost management section of the Organization Hub.
questions.stem: Which tiles are part of the Billing and Cost management section in the Organization Hub Insights dashboard? (Select THREE)

options.text: Cost by query type
Warehouse utilization percentage
Cost by service type
Contract utilization
Total cost
Credit consumption by user

explanation.correct: The Billing and Cost management section includes Total cost, Cost by service type, Total storage, and Contract utilization tiles. These display trends, breakdowns, and remaining capacity information.

distractors.A: Cost by query type is not a tile — cost is broken down by service type, not query type.
distractors.B: Warehouse utilization percentage is not a tile in the Billing and Cost management section.
distractors.F: Credit consumption by user is not a tile in the Billing and Cost management section.

questions.scenario: A user with any role in a Snowflake account wants to determine which organization their account belongs to, but they do not have the ORGADMIN or GLOBALORGADMIN role.
questions.stem: How can this user find the organization name of their current account?

options.text: Execute the CURRENT_ORGANIZATION_NAME function
Query the ORGANIZATIONS table in INFORMATION_SCHEMA
Execute SHOW ACCOUNTS to see the organization name
Contact their account administrator since only ORGADMIN can view this information

explanation.correct: Users with any role can execute the CURRENT_ORGANIZATION_NAME function to return the organization of the current account.

distractors.B: There is no ORGANIZATIONS table in INFORMATION_SCHEMA.
distractors.C: SHOW ACCOUNTS requires the ORGADMIN role or GLOBALORGADMIN role — regular users cannot execute it.
distractors.D: Any user can find their organization name using the CURRENT_ORGANIZATION_NAME function without needing elevated privileges.
